key_insight: FastFrames is a family of autoregressive video diffusion models designed to generate video at interactive latency without sacrificing quality. The central idea is to identify inference bottlenecks rather than accept the slow generation speeds of existing models.
problem_solved: Existing autoregressive video diffusion models are too slow for fluid interaction, limiting experiences where generated video must respond quickly to new observations or user inputs.
method: Profile the inference pipelines of state-of-the-art video generation models to locate performance bottlenecks.
Introduce FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that generate frames conditioned on new observations and inputs.
Target interactive latency while preserving output quality; specific optimizations and measurements are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: FastFrames could make responsive, AI-generated visual experiences more practical. For practitioners, it highlights inference-pipeline profiling as an important step toward low-latency video generation.
visual_elements: Feedback-loop diagram: user input → frame generation → displayed frame → next input.
Conceptual latency comparison between existing models and FastFrames, without unsupported numerical values.
Frame-strip illustration showing generated video adapting to changing inputs.
paper_title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
paper_authors: Gene Chou, Guandao Yang, Fujun Luan, Lars Mescheder, Wei Dong
